text: Play Snake on a 10 by 10 board. The blue head has a white arrow showing its direction; connected green segments form the body, fading lighter from neck to the pointed tail; only consecutive body segments are connected. The red circle is food. Each action moves one cell. Left and right turn relative to the current heading; straight keeps the heading. Eating food grows the snake. Hitting a wall or the body ends the game; the tail vacates its cell on a non-eating move. Identify which moves avoid an immediate collision. Use the CURRENT screenshot to adapt any earlier plan. For these diagnostic questions, safety means no wall or body collision on the next single move, not guaranteed long-term survival. Distinguish the pointed tail from other body segments. Entering the tail cell is safe on a non-eating move because it vacates simultaneously. No safe action means all three actions would collide on the next move; it does not mean a game-over screen is shown. Answer the current question even when an earlier strategy discusses food or long-term survival.
